method: WebSearch to identify candidate MoUs and summit coverage, then WebFetch to open and read primary/press sources for each candidate (including the Karnataka government's own official Invest Karnataka 2025 wrap-up press release PDF, dated 2025-02-14, fetched directly from investkarnataka.co.in). Company headquarters country checked against public company-profile knowledge. Only companies with a named, dated, sourced MoU are included; aggregate/undisclosed summit totals were not decomposed into unverified company entries. India-headquartered companies (including Indian-parented JVs and Indian real-estate/industrial groups) were excluded even where they appeared in the same MoU batches. Web search quota was exhausted partway through the sweep and several Deccan Herald / Business Standard article fetches returned HTTP 403; those leads are recorded in negative_notes rather than fabricated.

negative_notes: Foxconn's substantial, real Karnataka investments (e.g. Rs 8,800 cr mobile-components plan reported mid-2023, Rs 13,911 cr additional KIADB-approved investment) are excluded from this MoU list: available sources describe these as direct company announcements / state-cabinet or KIADB approvals rather than MoUs signed at a specific investor summit (Invest Karnataka or Davos). These likely belong in the twin's separate real-events layer (layer 42) rather than this MoU-graveyard-risk layer.

A widely-repeated claim of a 'Siemens Healthineers Rs 1,600 crore MoU at Davos' (surfaced in an initial broad web search) could NOT be independently corroborated with a dedicated, dated source. What was actually found: (a) a Rs 1,300 crore Bengaluru innovation-hub investment plan reported separately, (b) a Rs 313.20 crore Siemens Healthcare project cleared through Karnataka's normal project-approval process (270 jobs), and (c) an article describing Siemens Healthineers as still 'in talks' with the Karnataka government on healthtech/life-sciences Centres of Excellence (not a signed MoU). None of these cleanly matches the 'Rs 1,600 cr Davos MoU' claim, so it was excluded rather than reported as fact.

Web Werks, cited in some 'Davos 2024 Karnataka MoU' roundups for a Rs 20,000 crore, 100MW data-centre-park MoU, was excluded: Web Werks Data Centers is an India-headquartered company (Mumbai), not a foreign investor, despite being grouped with foreign companies (Microsoft, Hitachi, etc.) in secondary summaries of the same Davos 2024 delegation trip.

Karnataka's own official Invest Karnataka 2025 wrap-up (Feb 14, 2025) reports Rs 6,23,845 crore in MoUs signed and Rs 4,03,533 crore in investment commitments recognised/announced (total Rs 10,27,378 crore) -- but the 25 headline company-level announcements it itemizes sum to a small fraction of that total, and the great majority of even the itemized headline list (JSW Group, Baldota Steel & Power, Samvardhana Motherson, Emmvee Energy, RSOLEC, TASL/Tata, Wings Viterra, Balaji Wafers, Mahindra Susten, Hero Future Energies, Epsilon Group, Shree Cement, Havells, Suzlon Energy, TVS Motor Company) are India-headquartered and were correctly excluded from this foreign-company list per scope. The bulk of the aggregate GIM 2025 rupee total is therefore either Indian-company investment or undisclosed-company totals, not verifiable foreign-company MoUs -- a caution against treating the lakh-crore summit headline figures as a foreign-investment number.

Individual foreign-company names for the WEF Davos 2025 (Jan 2025) Karnataka delegation trip (reported aggregate figure: roughly Rs 13,070 crore across sectors including aerospace, food processing, data centres, digital infrastructure, clean energy and advanced manufacturing) could not be identified from the sources reached during this sweep; only the aggregate figure and sector list were found, so no individual MoU entries were added for this edition even though it is listed under summits_covered.

A Microsoft-Karnataka MoU at Davos 2024 was found but is a digital-skilling/workforce-development partnership, not an investment commitment, so it was left out of the mous list (which the task frames around investment MoUs); flagged here for completeness since Microsoft is a genuine foreign counterparty in a real, dated, named MoU.

An older, much larger ArcelorMittal MoU (~Rs 30,000 crore, six-million-tonne steel plant in Bellary district, signed at an earlier Karnataka Global Investors' Meet) was found via search but is from outside the 2021-2026 window (the source article context -- 'June 4' dateline referencing a two-day meet with then-CEO commentary -- indicates this is the well-known, long-stalled circa-2016-era Karnataka GIM MoU, a canonical example of the state's 'MoU graveyard' problem). It is excluded from this list as out-of-window, but is worth flagging as background: the same company (ArcelorMittal) has a documented history of large, unfulfilled Karnataka MoU commitments, which should inform skepticism toward its newer (2022, Rs 6,000 cr Vijayapura) MoU also listed here.

Search-tool web-search quota was exhausted partway through this sweep (200/200 calls used) and several Deccan Herald / Business Standard article URLs returned HTTP 403 on WebFetch. This constrained cross-verification of some entries (particularly the Davos-2022 batch, which relies on a single Deccan Herald source, and the ArcelorMittal follow-through question) to fewer independent sources than ideal. Confidence ratings reflect this.
